overall_summary: Analysis of recent performance on FACTVERSE shows a clear dominance of extreme space anomalies, hypothetical 'What If' planetary scenarios, and bizarre natural phenomena. Videos published within the last 7 days focusing on extreme cosmic destinations (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice worlds, dark exoplanets) achieve significantly higher views-per-day and like-to-view ratios compared to general psychology or older historical trivia. The highest velocity videos leverage curiosity-inducing 'What If' hypotheticals paired with astonishing visual destinations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 970 views rapidly with strong engagement (38 and 18 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive 'What If you fell into...' hooks using extreme cosmic objects as the setting.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) outperformed static historical or psychological trivia with over 1,000 and 700 views and exceptional engagement rates.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing fast-paced shorts featuring visually bizarre, scientifically accurate exoplanets and space weather.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5AN7LUgqarc) stalled under 100 views with negligible comment or like interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychology tips unless they feature an extreme, counter-intuitive biological shock value.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (yLm-FjYH6-k) plateaued quickly at 139 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague historical mystery hooks; if covering history, anchor it to a concrete, high-impact physical anomaly or survival scenario.
